cf.title: pg_walinspect: fix LSN validation messages and empty range handling

input.subject: pg_walinspect: fix LSN validation messages and empty range handling

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The patches reword error messages so they match checks that already accept equality, and change no check, SQLSTATE, catalog or format. The withdrawn v1-0002 was the only behaviour change. Confidence is medium because the code was not read and no committer has replied in the visible thread.

brief.title: Fix error messages that misstate inclusive bounds in pg_walinspect and core
brief.problem: Commit 5c1b6628075a relaxed pg_walinspect LSN checks to accept equality but left messages saying "must be less than". ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SKIP and psql's ParseVariableDouble() have the same mismatch between an inclusive check and a strict-sounding message. Users get error text that describes the wrong condition.
brief.proposed_design: Reword the messages to "less than or equal to" or "greater than or equal to" so they match the existing checks; no check changes. The second patch covers the two core sites and adds tests for the accepted boundary values. The original v1-0002, which returned zero rows for empty LSN ranges without starting a WAL reader, was withdrawn.
user_visible_surface: pg_walinspect error messages for input LSN versus current LSN, and start LSN versus end LSN, now say "less than or equal to".
ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SKIP error now says the skip LSN must be "greater than or equal to" the origin LSN.
psql variable range messages from ParseVariableDouble() (for example WATCH_INTERVAL) now describe inclusive [min,max] bounds.
author_claims: The message mismatch was an oversight in 5c1b6628075a.
The new wording matches wording used elsewhere in the tree.
Back-patching is not needed because the fix is not critical and the inaccuracy went unnoticed for years.
Current pg_walinspect documentation already allows an empty range to error when start_lsn is not available, so the empty-range change was dropped.
brief.thread_state: Kiran Kaki, Bharath Rupireddy, Surya Poondla and Xuneng Zhou reviewed and tested v5 and call it ready for committer. Bharath CC'd Michael on back-patching; no committer has replied.
unclear: No committer has said whether the core changes in 0002 belong in the same commit as the pg_walinspect fix.
The thread does not say whether translators need notice for the changed message strings.
The CommitFest entry targets "stable" while the commit message says not back-patched; the material does not reconcile this.
Surya's survey of other "must be less than" messages is the only check that no further sites need the same fix.
search_queries: error message less than or equal

prior_attempts.title: Fix for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW ownership error message
prior_attempts.quote: As the plan is not to backpatch, I’ll withdraw my patch.
prior_attempts.reason: Reviewers considered the change cosmetic and argued against back-patching: the existing message is not wrong, and changing behavior in released branches can affect applications that depend on the current text. While writing a regression test, the author found that HEAD/v11 already produced the correct message because of an earlier commit. With no back-patch planned, nothing was left to fix, and the author withdrew the patch.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P5 changed a message that was not wrong, and stopped once back-patching was ruled out. Here the messages misstate the inclusive checks on master, and the commit messages already say not back-patched.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch rewords the ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SKIP error in subscriptioncmds.c; the check itself does not change.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: ParseVariableDouble() range messages in psql/variables.c change, for example for WATCH_INTERVAL.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets "stable" while the commit message says not back-patched.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Changed message strings need new translations and affect anyone who matches on the error text.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Should the CommitFest target be changed from "stable" to match the commit message, which says the fix is not back-patched?
Should 0002, which touches subscriptioncmds.c and psql, go in a separate commit and thread subject from the pg_walinspect fix?
Beyond Surya's survey of "must be less than" messages, were "must be greater than" and similar strict wordings also checked against their comparisons?

committability.owner_note: Any committer can own the message changes; one who knows pg_walinspect or logical replication would confirm the checks are meant to be inclusive. Michael was CC'd on back-patching but has not replied.
committability.liability: Small: a few changed message strings on master and two new boundary tests. The owner signs for the wording matching the checks and for the new tests being stable.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered reviews promptly, withdrew 0002 on his own finding, and posted five versions in about a month.

priority.reason: Two patches of about 6 KiB each change only message text and tests, and four reviewers call v5 ready for committer. Few users hit these boundary errors, but the cost of committing is also small.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so it is unverified that each reworded message matches its comparison and that no other site has the same mismatch. Stability of the new boundary tests in subscription.sql and 001_basic.pl was also not checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Mention column name in error messages
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the target column name to errors raised when a value cannot be coerced to a column's type in INSERT or ALTER COLUMN, for example "value too long for type character varying(4)". After review, the first version, which changed datatype input functions, was reworked to use an error context callback in the parser.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund reviewed the patch and asked for code cleanups and tests, since the patch had none. The author did not reply, and Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback two months after that review because the comments had not been addressed.

precedents_retrieved.title: Re: MarkBufferDirtyHint() and LSN update
precedents_retrieved.summary: Michael Paquier's patch, built on a race Antonin Houska reported, makes MarkBufferDirtyHint() set the page LSN even when BM_DIRTY is already set. The race is that FlushBuffer() has written the page but not yet cleared BM_DIRTY, so a later flush can write the hint-bit change without its WAL record having been flushed first.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier found that the patch lets page LSNs go backwards. He reproduced this with checksums enabled, shared_buffers at 1MB and pgbench, because a page can get a newer LSN before the LSN returned by XLogSaveBufferForHint() is set. Antonin Houska proposed an extra diff on top, but the visible messages do not show why the entry was then withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I have been studying more the patch,
and after stressing more this code path with a cluster having
checksums enabled and shared_buffers at 1MB, I have been able to make
a couple of page's LSNs go backwards with pgbench -s 100.

precedents_retrieved.title: Mention column name in error messages
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the target column name and type to errors raised when a value is coerced into an insert or update column, such as "value too long for type character varying(4)". After review it used an error context callback set up during parse analysis of assigned expressions instead of changing datatype input functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found that the callback only covers errors raised during parse analysis or constant folding, not run-time errors from non-constant expressions, and covering those would need executor changes with a likely performance cost. He argued that partial coverage would mislead users and that the cases it handles already have error cursor information. He proposed extending error cursor support into execution instead, and Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If it isn't,
we'd be best off to reject this patch rather than create an expectation
among users that such context should be there.

precedents_retrieved.title: LSN Map
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a new relation fork ("lm") that stores the maximum LSN for each group of 2048 heap blocks (16 MB), so incremental backup can skip unchanged ranges without reading the blocks. The map is updated each time a heap page's LSN changes and is not WAL-logged.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas objected that updating the map on every page change doubles buffer manager traffic and makes all backends contend for the exclusive lock on a single LSN map page. He also wanted the update done in common code such as PageSetLSN or XLogInsert, since each index AM would otherwise have to update the map itself. Tom Lane asked for measurements showing the 16 MB summary saves enough backup work, and no measurements were posted. In July, with no new version after Robert Haas suggested a background process that reads WAL, Heikki marked the entry Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch doubles the buffer manager traffic, because any update to any page will also need to modify the LSN map.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix for REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW ownership error message
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW so that a permission failure reports "must be owner of materialized view" instead of the generic "must be owner of relation", by passing OBJECT_MATVIEW to the ACL check error path. The author offered to prepare back-patches for released branches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers considered the change cosmetic and argued against back-patching: the existing message is not wrong, and changing behavior in released branches can affect applications that depend on the current text. While writing a regression test, the author found that HEAD/v11 already produced the correct message because of an earlier commit. With no back-patch planned, nothing was left to fix, and the author withdrew the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: As the plan is not to backpatch, I’ll withdraw my patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: NLS: use gettext() to translate system error messages
precedents_retrieved.summary: Translate the system error text substituted for %m with gettext and Postgres's own .po files, instead of relying on strerror_r() translation. This makes errno messages follow NLS on every platform and stops depending on LC_CTYPE.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that platforms whose strerror() does not translate leave their users used to untranslated errno strings, so Postgres should behave like other programs on the platform. He also objected to putting the translation in snprintf.c and noted that the implementation was not thread-safe. The author marked the entry rejected because there was no consensus to proceed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If it doesn't, then the users of that platform are unaccustomed to
seeing translated errno strings, and they are unlikely to thank us
for behaving differently from every other program on the platform.

precedents_retrieved.title: Align verify_heapam.c error message offset with test expectations
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes three error messages in contrib/amcheck/verify_heapam.c to report the successor tuple's offset (nextoffnum) instead of the current line pointer (ctx.offnum). A second part tightens the pg_amcheck test 004_verify_heapam.pl to expect the exact offset 43 instead of a \d+ wildcard.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Two reviewers agreed with the code fix, and no one objected. The author said he would not revise the test change further and left the decision to committers, and the thread ends there.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add LSN <-> time conversion facility
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an LSNTimeStream, a fixed-size structure in the WAL stats that bgwriter fills with (LSN, timestamp) points and thins over time. SQL functions use it to convert between LSN and time, and it was meant as a base for an opportunistic freezing heuristic.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No message states why the entry was withdrawn, but the thread ended with the design unresolved. Tomas Vondra and Robert Haas questioned keeping the data in pgstat, because stats are lost on crash, reset or standby promotion, and no one proposed a clear alternative. They also asked for a simple, known thinning method with better accuracy for recent LSNs. The author then chose to shape the structure for the freezing patch first and moved her work there.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Actually, I think this is a hard problem in terms of where to actually store the data -- as Tomas said, pgstat doesn't seem quite right, and it's not clear to me what is actually right.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Get rid of the dedicated latch for signaling the startup process".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Get rid of the dedicated latch for signaling the startup process".
Reverted commit(s): Get rid of the dedicated latch for signaling the startup process.; Fix segmentation fault that commit ac22929a26 caused.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert ac22929a26, as well as the followup fix 113d3591b8. Because it broke
the assumption that the startup process waiting for the recovery conflict
on buffer pin should be waken up only by buffer unpin or the timeout enabled
in ResolveRecoveryConflictWithBufferPin(). It caused, for example,
SIGHUP signal handler or walreceiver process to wake that startup process
up unnecessarily frequently.

Additionally, add the comments about why that dedicated latch that
the reverted patch tried to get rid of should not be removed.

Thanks to Kyotaro Horiguchi for the discussion.

roaster_notes.note: The only precedent, [P5], died over back-patching a cosmetic message change; this proposal fixes wrong text on master only, so that reason does not apply. The withdrawn empty-range change (message #3) was dropped by the author, and the thread cites no earlier attempt at either change.

The patches change only error message text to match existing checks, keep the SQLSTATE, and go to master only, so no query, dump or client sees different behaviour. The 'stable' target in the CommitFest entry conflicts with the commit message, but no back-patch is planned, and [P5] advises against one anyway.

The proposal changes only error message text in pg_walinspect, ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SKIP and psql, and adds tests. It touches no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol message or extension ABI, and the withdrawn v1-0002 was the only behaviour change. Changed message strings matter only for translators and for anyone matching error text, which is outside this angle.

The patch only rewords error messages so they match existing inclusive checks. It changes no check, privilege, default or exposed data. The messages already reported the same LSN values before, so no new information leaks. The new subscription test runs as the existing superuser test role and grants nothing new.

From the maintenance angle there is nothing to object to. The patch rewords error messages to match checks already in the tree, adds no GUC, catalog change, API or hot-path work, and uses wording that already exists in core. Translators get the usual string churn of a major release. [P5] objected to back-patching a cosmetic message change, and this proposal is not back-patched, so [P5] does not apply. The CommitFest target of "stable" disagrees with the commit message, which is a tracking mismatch, not a design problem. No committer has engaged yet, but a fix this small needs little expertise to own.

The proposal rewords error messages so they match checks already in core and in pg_walinspect. No existing feature, extension or tool gives users an accurate message, so there is nothing for this angle to point to. [P5] was about cosmetic back-patching of a message that was not wrong; here the messages are wrong, and the patch is not back-patched.

The demand test does not fit here. The patch rewords error messages that describe the wrong condition, adds no feature, and changes no check. The only cost is translator churn on a few strings, and correct error text helps every user who hits these errors. [P5] objected to a cosmetic change and to back-patching it; this proposal fixes inaccurate text and is not back-patched.
